Key Research Thinking Patterns: Computational Complexity-Driven Algorithm Design: Establishing NP-Hardness via reductions from Knapsack and MAX-2SAT problems to justify the development of iterative and greedy approximation algorithms for switching cost and utility optimization.

Hybrid Epidemiological-Network Optimization: Integrating Susceptible-Infected-Recovered (SIR) models with Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) to simulate and interdict the cascading spread of disinformation across interdependent information-physical networks.

Stochastic Utility Maximization under Uncertainty: Employing expectation operators and decay functions within Integer Linear Programming (ILP) frameworks to optimize resource scheduling and network robustness against probabilistic failures and adversarial manipulations.

Causal Failure Propagation Modeling: Utilizing causality graphs and multi-commodity flow theory to map and mitigate cascading failures in complex systems such as urban power grids and transit networks under demand-response manipulation.
Summary Description: Sridhar Radhakrishnan specializes in stochastic optimization and cyber-physical security, focusing on the resilience of critical infrastructure against cascading failures and weaponized disinformation. He bridges theoretical computer science and operations research by employing Integer Linear Programming (ILP) and Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) to model dynamic utility functions and causal link failures. His work integrates epidemiological models, such as SIR, with network optimization to interdict disinformation campaigns affecting power grids and transit systems. By proving NP-Hardness and developing greedy approximations, he addresses complex resource allocation in disaster management and defense. His research ensures system functionality under uncertainty, leveraging real-world datasets from NYC subway and Swedish rail networks to mitigate adversarial impacts on societal stability.
